breakfast.name: Baleadas
instructions: Warm thick flour tortillas on griddle
Spread with refried beans
Add cream, cheese, eggs, avocado
Fold in half
breakfast.description: Honduras's most beloved food — thick tortillas with beans and cream.

breakfast.name: Plátanos con Frijoles
instructions: Slice and fry plantains
Serve with refried beans and cream
breakfast.description: Fried plantains with beans and cream.

breakfast.name: Baleadas (Honduras's National Breakfast)
ingredients: Crema (Honduran sour cream — thicker than Mexican)
instructions: Make thick, soft flour tortillas — larger than Mexican tortillas, softer
Spread generous refried beans on one half
Add thick Honduran crema — it's richer and thicker than Mexican crema
Crumble queso seco on top — the salty-dry cheese is key
Add scrambled eggs, chorizo, or avocado for the 'especial' version
Fold in half — do not roll like a burrito
Eat immediately while warm — the tortilla must be soft
Baleadas are Honduras's #1 food — eaten for breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack
Every Honduran has a baleada opinion — the best vendor, the right fillings
Simple baleada (beans, crema, cheese) vs. especial (add everything)
breakfast.description: Honduras's national food — a large soft flour tortilla folded over refried beans, thick crema, and crumbled dry cheese. Every Honduran eats baleadas. Every Honduran has a baleada opinion. The simple-vs-especial debate and the perfect-fold technique are viral Honduran food content.

breakfast.name: Plato Típico (Honduran Typical Plate)
instructions: Cook refried beans — red beans mashed and fried with onion
Make white rice
Fry ripe plantain slices until golden and caramelized
Fry or scramble eggs
Arrange everything on one plate: beans, rice, plantain, egg
Add crema, crumbled cheese, avocado
Serve with warm tortillas on the side
Every element is simple; together they are complete
This is how Honduras starts the day — everything on one plate
The plato típico is the base layer of Honduran food identity
breakfast.description: Honduras's typical breakfast plate — refried beans, rice, fried sweet plantain, eggs, crema, cheese, and tortillas all on one plate. Simple individually, complete together. This is the foundational plate of Honduran food identity.

breakfast.name: Catrachas (Fried Tortilla with Beans and Cheese)
instructions: Fry corn tortillas in oil until crispy — like a flat tostada
Spread refried beans on the crispy tortilla
Top with crumbled queso seco
Add crema
Add curtido (pickled cabbage) if desired
The name 'catrachas' is also the nickname for Hondurans — 'catracho/catracha'
This is Honduras's simplest and most identity-defining snack
The crispy-bean-cheese combination is the same in every Honduran home
breakfast.description: Catrachas — fried tortillas topped with beans and cheese, named after the word Hondurans call themselves (catrachos). Honduras's identity on a crispy tortilla. The simplest expression of Honduran food and the most culturally loaded.

lunch.name: Sopa de Caracol (Conch Soup)
instructions: Tenderize and dice conch
Sauté garlic, onion, chili
Add coconut milk and water
Add conch, plantain, yuca, green banana
Simmer 30 min
Add cilantro and lime
lunch.description: Coconut-based conch soup — Garífuna heritage dish.

lunch.name: Tapado (Seafood Soup)
instructions: Sauté garlic, tomatoes, chili
Add coconut milk and water
Add seafood and root vegetables
Simmer 20 min
Garnish with cilantro

lunch.name: Sopa de Caracol (Conch Soup)
instructions: Tenderize conch by pounding — it's tough if not properly prepared
Cut conch into pieces, boil until tender — 30-40 min with lime juice
Make broth: sauté onion, garlic, bell pepper, add coconut milk and water
Add yuca and green plantain — cook until tender
Add the tender conch to the coconut broth
Season with Scotch bonnet, cilantro, lime juice
The soup should be creamy-white from the coconut milk
The Garífuna people of Honduras's north coast created this soup
There's a famous Honduran song called 'Sopa de Caracol' — it went viral globally in the 90s
The song made the soup famous worldwide — and the soup deserves every bit of the fame
lunch.description: Honduras's legendary conch soup — conch simmered in coconut milk with yuca and plantain, created by the Garífuna people of the north coast. Made world-famous by the 1991 hit song 'Sopa de Caracol' that went viral across Latin America. The song-food connection makes this one of the most culturally storied dishes in the Americas.

lunch.name: Tapado (Garífuna Seafood Coconut Stew)
ingredients: Mixed seafood: fish, shrimp, crab, conch
instructions: Make rich fish stock from fish bones
Add coconut milk — generous, this is a coconut-based stew
Add green and ripe plantain, yuca — cook until tender
Add seafood in stages: fish first, then shrimp and crab (they cook faster)
Add Scotch bonnet, cilantro, lime juice
The stew should be creamy-white, thick with coconut and loaded with seafood
This is Garífuna celebration food — the Afro-Caribbean people of Honduras's coast
The Garífuna are UNESCO-recognized — their food is living heritage
Tapado showcases the entire sea — every seafood in one pot
Serve in large bowls with extra coconut broth for soaking
lunch.description: Garífuna tapado — a coconut milk seafood stew loaded with fish, shrimp, crab, and conch alongside plantain and yuca. Created by the Garífuna people (UNESCO-recognized living heritage) of Honduras's Caribbean coast. The 'entire ocean in coconut milk' concept is viral Caribbean food storytelling.

lunch.name: Pollo con Tajadas (Fried Chicken with Fried Plantain)
ingredients: Lime juice, garlic, cumin, salt, pepper
Green plantain (sliced thin lengthwise — tajadas, not rounds)
instructions: Season chicken with lime, garlic, cumin, salt — marinate 30 min
Fry chicken until golden and cooked through — 12-15 min
Slice green plantain lengthwise into thin strips — tajadas
Fry tajadas until golden and crispy
Make curtido: pickled cabbage with vinegar, onion, oregano
Plate: fried chicken on a bed of tajadas, topped with curtido
Add ketchup and mustard — this is how Honduras does it
Tajadas are the long thin plantain chips — not the round ones
This is Honduras's fried chicken — and it's a lifestyle, not just food
lunch.description: Honduras's fried chicken and tajadas — crispy chicken served on a bed of long, thin fried green plantain strips topped with pickled cabbage. The tajadas (thin plantain strips, not rounds) are uniquely Honduran and the ketchup-mustard condiment combo is non-negotiable.

dinner.name: Carne Asada Hondureña
instructions: Marinate beef in lime, garlic, cumin
Grill over charcoal until medium
Slice thin
Serve with chimol, tortillas, and beans
dinner.description: Grilled, marinated beef — Honduran cookout staple.

dinner.name: Pollo con Tajadas (Chicken with Fried Plantain)
instructions: Marinate chicken in achiote, garlic, lime
Fry or roast chicken until golden
Slice and fry green plantains
Serve together with curtido
dinner.description: Achiote chicken with crispy green plantain chips.

dinner.name: Nacatamales (Honduran Giant Tamales)
instructions: Make enriched masa dough — softer and richer than regular masa
Cook filling: meat in tomato sauce with garlic, onion, sweet pepper
Prepare banana leaves: pass over flame to soften
Spread generous amount of masa on banana leaf — much more than a regular tamale
Layer: masa, meat, rice, potato, olives, capers
The filling is elaborate — this is not a simple tamale
Wrap tightly in banana leaf, tie with string — they're large parcels
Boil for 2+ hours until masa is firm and cooked through
These are LARGE — meal-sized, not snack-sized
Nacatamales are Saturday-Sunday food — the whole family helps assemble
Traditionally eaten for breakfast with coffee — yes, this giant tamale for breakfast
dinner.description: Honduras's giant tamales — massive banana-leaf-wrapped parcels of enriched masa filled with meat, rice, potatoes, olives, and capers, boiled for 2+ hours. Nacatamales are a family-assembly-line weekend tradition. The size (meal-sized, not snack-sized), the elaborate filling, and the weekend-ritual aspect are viral.

dinner.name: Enchiladas Hondureñas (Honduran Enchiladas)
instructions: Fry corn tortillas flat until crispy — these are NOT rolled like Mexican enchiladas
Spread tomato sauce on the crispy tortilla
Top with seasoned ground beef
Add sliced hard-boiled egg
Top with curtido (pickled cabbage), crumbled cheese, avocado
The Honduran enchilada is essentially a loaded tostada — flat and open-faced
Every ingredient is layered on top — nothing is rolled or folded
The hard-boiled egg on top is the Honduran signature — don't skip it
These are Honduras's loaded crispy tortillas — sharing only the name with Mexican enchiladas
dinner.description: Honduran enchiladas — nothing like the Mexican version. These are flat fried tortillas stacked high with ground beef, boiled egg, pickled cabbage, and cheese. The name confusion between Honduran and Mexican enchiladas is a perpetual food-internet debate and viral content.

dinner.name: Sopa de Mondongo (Tripe Soup)
instructions: Clean tripe thoroughly — soak in lime juice, scrub, rinse multiple times
Boil tripe (and cow's foot if using) for 2+ hours until tender
The broth becomes rich and gelatinous from the collagen
Add root vegetables: yuca, potato, carrots — cook until tender
Add green plantain, cabbage in the last 15 min
Season with oregano, cumin, Scotch bonnet
Finish with lime juice and fresh cilantro
The soup should be thick, rich, deeply flavored from the long cooking
Mondongo is Honduras's hangover cure and Sunday tradition
The preparation is long but the result is worth every hour
dinner.description: Honduras's tripe soup — beef tripe slow-cooked for hours into a rich, gelatinous, deeply flavored broth loaded with root vegetables and plantain. The Sunday tradition, the hangover-cure reputation, and the 'it takes 3 hours but it's worth it' dedication make mondongo viral comfort food.

snacks.name: Pastelitos de Carne
ingredients: Filling: ground beef, potatoes, rice, peas
instructions: Make masa dough
Fill with meat mixture
Shape, seal edges
Deep fry until golden
snacks.description: Fried corn dough turnovers with meat and potatoes.

snacks.name: Pastelitos de Carne (Fried Meat Turnovers)
ingredients: Dough: flour, butter, egg, water, salt
Filling: seasoned ground beef or rice with chicken
instructions: Make dough: flour, butter, egg, water — work until smooth, rest
Make filling: brown ground beef with onion, garlic, cumin, tomato sauce
Roll out dough, cut into circles
Fill with meat mixture, fold into half-moons, seal edges with fork
Deep fry until golden — 3-4 min
Drain briefly, serve hot
The crust should be flaky and slightly blistered
These are Honduras's party food — no celebration without pastelitos
The rice-and-chicken version is equally popular as the beef
Serve with ketchup — yes, ketchup
snacks.description: Honduran meat turnovers — flaky fried pockets filled with spiced ground beef or rice-and-chicken. Essential at every Honduran party, birthday, and celebration. The ketchup dip and the flaky crust make pastelitos Honduras's favorite hand-held party food.

snacks.name: Yuca con Chicharrón (Yuca with Fried Pork)
ingredients: Chicharrón (fried pork skin or fried pork belly)
instructions: Boil yuca until fork-tender — 15-20 min
Fry chicharrón until crispy and golden — or buy it pre-made
The yuca should be soft and starchy inside
Serve yuca topped with crispy chicharrón
Add curtido (pickled cabbage) on top
Squeeze lime over everything
The soft, starchy yuca against the crispy, salty pork is the contrast
This is Honduras's most satisfying snack — carb and protein in perfect balance
Sold at every street stall and market in Honduras
snacks.description: Yuca with chicharrón — soft boiled cassava topped with crispy fried pork and pickled cabbage. Starchy-soft meets salty-crispy in Honduras's most satisfying street snack. The texture contrast and the lime-curtido finish are street food perfection.

desserts.name: Torrejas (Honduran French Toast)
instructions: Make panela syrup with cinnamon and cloves
Dip bread in beaten eggs
Fry until golden
Drench in panela syrup
desserts.description: Fried bread soaked in panela syrup — a Holy Week treat.

desserts.name: Tres Leches Cake (Honduran Style)
ingredients: Sponge cake: flour, eggs, sugar, vanilla
Three milks: condensed milk, evaporated milk, heavy cream
instructions: Make light sponge cake: beat eggs with sugar until tripled in volume, fold in flour
Bake at 175°C until golden and springy — 25-30 min
Let cool, poke holes all over with a fork — the holes are essential
Mix the three milks: condensed, evaporated, heavy cream, add cinnamon
Pour the milk mixture over the cake — slowly, letting it absorb
Refrigerate overnight — the cake soaks up all the milk
The next day: the cake is impossibly moist, almost pudding-like
Top with whipped cream, dust with cinnamon
Add cherries if desired
Tres leches is Central America's shared dessert — Honduras claims it proudly
desserts.description: Tres leches cake — sponge cake soaked in three milks until impossibly moist, topped with whipped cream. The overnight soaking transforms a light cake into a milk-drenched, pudding-like dessert. Central America's most famous sweet, and Honduras makes one of the best versions.

desserts.name: Torrejas (Honduran French Toast)
ingredients: Dulce de panela (raw cane sugar syrup)
instructions: Make panela syrup: dissolve raw cane sugar in water with cinnamon, cloves — boil until syrupy
Soak bread in milk, then dip in beaten egg
Fry in oil or butter until golden on both sides
Drench the fried bread in warm panela syrup — soak it
The syrup should be thick, dark, and spiced
The bread should be custardy inside, crispy outside, swimming in syrup
Torrejas are Holy Week food — eaten during Semana Santa across Honduras
The panela syrup (not maple syrup) is what makes this Central American
Every grandmother's torrejas are 'the best'
desserts.description: Honduran torrejas — fried egg-dipped bread drenched in warm spiced raw-cane-sugar syrup. Honduras's Holy Week tradition. The dark panela syrup (not maple) and the custardy-inside, syrup-soaked result make torrejas Central America's most indulgent version of French toast.

drinks.name: Horchata de Morro
instructions: Toast and grind seeds and rice
Boil with cocoa and spices
Strain, sweeten
Serve cold

drinks.name: Licuado de Banana
instructions: Blend all ingredients until smooth
Serve cold

drinks.name: Horchata Hondureña (Morro Seed Drink)
instructions: Toast morro seeds and rice until fragrant — this step is essential
Grind together into a fine powder — traditionally in a grinding stone
Mix the powder with water — stir until dissolved
Add cinnamon, vanilla, sugar
Strain through a fine cloth
Serve ice cold
Honduran horchata is NOT the same as Mexican horchata (which is rice-only)
The morro (jícaro) seeds give a unique, nuttier flavor
The jícaro tree is Central America's 'gourd tree' — the fruit is iconic
drinks.description: Honduran horchata — NOT the Mexican version. Made from toasted jícaro (morro) seeds and rice, creating a nuttier, more complex drink. The jícaro tree is iconic to Central America and this drink is Honduras's refreshment of choice.

drinks.name: Café de Olla (Clay Pot Coffee)
ingredients: Honduran coffee (Honduras is a top-10 global coffee producer)
instructions: Heat water in a clay pot (olla de barro) — the clay adds flavor
Add panela, cinnamon stick, cloves — let dissolve
Add ground coffee directly to the pot
Bring to a simmer — do not boil
Let steep 5 min, strain
The clay pot adds a mineral, earthy flavor that metal can't replicate
Honduras produces some of the world's finest coffee — this is the traditional way to drink it
The sweetness from panela (not refined sugar) and the spices transform plain coffee
This is how coffee is drunk in the Honduran campo (countryside)
drinks.description: Honduran clay-pot coffee — fresh-ground Honduran coffee brewed with raw cane sugar and cinnamon in a clay pot. Honduras is a top-10 global coffee producer, and café de olla is how the countryside has drunk it for centuries. The clay-pot technique and the 'coffee country' origin make this viral.
